title: AI Finds Thousands of Hidden Steps for Turning CO2 Into Fuel
summary:
Carbon dioxide, or CO2, is a gas that comes from burning fuels. Scientists want to turn it into useful things, like a fuel called methanol. Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science used artificial intelligence, or AI, to help.

To change CO2, scientists mix it with hydrogen and use a helper material called a catalyst. In this study, the catalyst was copper. The change happens in many tiny steps called reactions.

The team started with 152 reactions. Then their AI helped them find many more, for a total of 9,389.

The bigger list worked much better. The small list gave the wrong answer about what would be made. The big list matched real experiments and predicted about 40 times more CO2 being changed.

The team also found a surprise. Hydrogen could sometimes join in as a whole molecule instead of splitting apart first. This could help scientists design better catalysts.
why_it_matters: Finding new ways to turn a waste gas into fuel could help scientists make useful things from something we usually throw away.
